title: MLX's in-process JIT runs the emitted Metal route bit-identically on family7, but cannot express two of the three compile commitments the Swift host sets
executor_revision: not applicable: the bounded tools/metal correctness harness runs without an Executor; the checkout's current family7 Executor is open-cake-ir-b200-v113+3d17b096a0d91baa5dfdf2698b9435c1de956803b10b297ba772df105943f9b6

evidence.note: 95 cases over four operators, five shapes and four or five input distributions, each prepared once by tools/metal/adapter.py and then run twice: once through the Swift runner's MTLDevice.makeLibrary and once through mx.fast.metal_kernel. Both hosts passed the same external oracle and every output buffer was byte-identical between them; differential.json carries the per-case comparisons and driver.py the exact matrix. MLX 0.32.0, Apple M1 Pro, applegpu_g13s.

The same 95-case matrix repeated on MLX 0.32.2 after it was installed into the checkout's own .venv, again 95 of 95 byte-identical to the Swift host. Two MLX minor versions agreeing narrows the risk that the result depends on one build's compile defaults, but still covers only this target and this operator set.

One case's retained receipt and bridged source. mlx-bridge.metal is the emitted kernel.metal minus its signature, with two alias statements restoring `program` and `lane`; runtime.stdout.json records grid [128,1,1] under dispatchThreads against the emitted [4,1,1] threadgroups, and names unset_compile_options and unchecked_pipeline_commitments.

observation: runner.swift sets three MTLCompileOptions: languageVersion .version2_3, mathMode .safe and mathFloatingPointFunctions .precise, and then refuses a pipeline whose threadExecutionWidth, staticThreadgroupMemoryLength or maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup differ from the manifest. mx.fast.metal_kernel accepts math_mode alone and returns arrays rather than the MTLComputePipelineState, so an MLX host sets one of the three options and can check none of the three pipeline commitments. On this corpus the two unset options changed nothing: all 95 outputs were byte-identical to the Swift host's. That is a bound on these four FP32 single-SIMD-group operators at family7, not a general equivalence, and the emitted body already spells `precise::` on every transcendental it uses, so the result is consistent with the options being redundant here rather than with them being unnecessary. Two mechanical differences are required and were confirmed: MLX dispatches threads where the Swift host dispatches threadgroups, so the first grid axis is multiplied by the 32-lane threadgroup, and MLX generates the signature itself from input_names/output_names, so the emitted preamble must be handed over as `header` and the position attributes re-aliased in the body. A header whose last line is a `//` comment and lacks a trailing newline silently comments out the signature MLX generates; that produced 95 compile failures inside MLX's own utils.h before it was found. MLX keys its compiled-kernel cache on the source and not only on the kernel name, so a second shape of one entry point recompiles rather than silently reusing the first. This host is not the sealed binary-archive path: it performs no archive reload, seals no LaunchableCandidate, and cannot observe input-buffer mutation because MLX owns the input allocations.
proposed_change: Keep MLX as a second host for the bounded tools/metal correctness harness (`check_correctness.py --host mlx`), not as a lowering route. It removes the Swift host build from that loop and gives the same emitted source an independent compiler and launcher, which is a differential the single-host harness could not produce. Do not propose an `mlx` Compiler lowering route on this evidence: a route would have to declare compile commitments the backend cannot set, and AGENTS.md requires a full Corpus Gate and independent ADR 0052 approval for a new backend. Revisit only if a later finding needs a Metal host where the Swift toolchain is unavailable, which F-2026-09-13-001 no longer is.
verification_plan: Replay: re-run the same 95-case differential on the successor Revision and require every output to stay byte-identical across the two hosts. Widen before relying on it further: multi-SIMD-group schedules, which declare threadgroup storage and which the bridge currently refuses, and the family8/family9 exact devices, which no measurement here covers.
